confidence_self_assessment.rationale: Strong attestation backbone (45/50 terms with k_en>=4 AND k_zh>=4). The 5 keep_kunder4 exceptions (mens rea, actus reus, felony, parole, conspiracy to defraud) are foundational common-law doctrinal categories whose statutory under-attestation is principled, not artefactual: mens rea / actus reus are judge-made categories rarely surfaced verbatim in Cap. ordinances; felony has been formally displaced by 'indictable offence' in HK statutes; parole is administered via a Review-Board apparatus that uses peripheral lexicalisations; conspiracy_to_defraud is a common-law inchoate doctrine whose Chinese forms in indictments are composite. Sub-area balance achieved: substantive_offences=10, sentencing=10, elements=10, other=10, classifications=6, defences=2, inchoate=2. The two thin sub-areas (defences, inchoate) reflect a genuine HK Cap. surface scarcity: defences (duress, necessity, self-defence, automatism) live primarily in case law; inchoate offences other than conspiracy/conspiracy-to-defraud are statutorily formulated as substantive offences under Cap. 200. Promotions favour high knn_confidence (>=0.85) where doctrinally unambiguous; lower-confidence promotions (0.57) selected on doctrinal centrality (e.g. arrestable, terrorist, fraudulent).

weakest_decisions.concern: 'deliberately' (elements) is morphologically adjacent to 'intent' and 'knowingly'; retained as canonical statutory adverbial formulator but borderline against the near-synonym consolidation rule.

'terrorist' classified as classifications rather than other; defensible under Cap. 575 (statutory designation), but the boundary between 'subject category' and 'offender category' is doctrinally fluid.

'corruption' classified as 'other' rather than 'substantive_offences'; the Cap. 201 framework makes it a substantive-offence umbrella, but the 10-cap on substantive_offences forced the bucket-shift. Doctrinally the term is hybrid (umbrella / category).
'detained' classified as sentencing rather than other; pre-trial detention is procedural, post-conviction detention is sentencing. The single term spans both readings.

'deception' classified as elements (act-element of fraud) rather than substantive_offences; defensible since Cap. 210 ss.17-18A treat deception as the conduct-element predicate, but the bucket choice was constrained by the substantive_offences cap.

notes: Curation respects a hard attestation gate (k_en>=4 AND k_zh>=4 in HK Cap. e-Legislation) for 45/50 terms, with 5 doctrinally indispensable exceptions documented under keep_kunder4. Sub-area coverage: all six listed sub-areas are non-empty. Defences (k=2) and inchoate (k=2) are intentionally thin: HK common-law defences (self-defence, duress, necessity, insanity) live in case law and are weakly surfaced in Cap. ordinances; statutory inchoate offences are largely subsumed into substantive-offence definitions in Cap. 200. The 'other' bucket (k=10, at the cap) collects criminal-justice actors and process terms (arrest, conviction, prosecutor, jury, verdict, accessory, ICAC, arraignment) that do not fit the six listed sub-areas but are doctrinally indispensable. Drops include morphological derivatives (criminal_law, penal, accomplice/accessory pair, blackmail/extortion overlap), historical common-law terms displaced in HK statute (larceny, robbery, burglary), institutional/scheme names with k=0/0 (Sexual Conviction Record Check Scheme, going equipped for burglary), and procedure-adjacent terms better placed in the procedure domain (indictment, prosecution, remand, DPP).
